questions.question: Start at 12, add 4 each time. What is the 4th number?
questions.explain: Start at 12 and add 4 three times: 12, 16, 20, 24. You only add 4 three times to reach the 4th number, not four times.

questions.question: Start at 15, add 6 each time. What is the 3rd number?
questions.explain: Start at 15 and add 6 two times: 15, 21, 27. The 3rd number needs two additions, not three.

questions.question: Start at 6, add 20 each time. What is the 3rd number?
questions.explain: Start at 6 and add 20 two times: 6, 26, 46. Be careful not to swap the start number (6) with the change (20).

questions.question: Start at 7, add 5 each time. What is the 4th number?
questions.explain: Start at 7 and add 5 three times: 7, 12, 17, 22. You add 5 three times to get the 4th number, not four times.

questions.question: Maya saves 8 dollars each week. She starts with 3 dollars. How much does she have after the 3rd week?
questions.explain: Maya starts with 3 and saves 8 three times: 3, 11, 19, 27. After 3 weeks she has saved 3 times, not 4.

questions.question: A recipe says to add 9 grams of sugar each time. You start with 4 grams. After adding it 3 more times, how much sugar do you have?
questions.explain: You start with 4 grams and add 9 three times: 4, 13, 22, 31. Add 9 only three times, not four.

questions.question: A water tank gets 15 litres each hour. It starts with 10 litres. How many litres are in the tank after 4 hours?
questions.explain: The tank starts at 10 L and gets 15 L four times: 10, 25, 40, 55, 70. After 4 hours you add 15 four times, not five.

questions.question: The rule is: start at 6, add 8. First find the 4th number in the pattern. Then add 3 more. What do you get?
questions.explain: The 4th number is 6, 14, 22, 30. Then add 3 more to get 33. The common trap is adding 8 four times instead of three.

questions.question: The rule is: start at 15, add 12. What is the 5th number in the pattern?
questions.explain: Start at 15 and add 12 four times: 15, 27, 39, 51, 63. The 5th number needs four additions, not five.

questions.question: The rule is: start at 3, add 5. A student writes the pattern as 5, 8, 11, 14. What went wrong?
options: They added 5 one extra time at the start.
They swapped the start and the change.
They multiplied 5 by the position number.
questions.explain: The student started at 5 and added 3 — that is the change and the start swapped. The rule says start at 3 and add 5, giving 3, 8, 13, 18.

questions.question: The rule is: start at 8, add 6. What is the 6th number in the pattern?
questions.explain: Start at 8 and add 6 five times: 8, 14, 20, 26, 32, 38. The 6th number needs five additions, not six.

questions.question: Lin's bean plant is 4 cm tall today. It grows 7 cm each week. How tall will it be after 3 weeks?
questions.explain: Start at 4, then add 7 three times: 11, 18, 25. The plant is 25 cm tall. Stopping at 18 means you only grew it for two weeks.

questions.question: At a bake sale, the first table has 5 muffins. Each table after that has 10 more muffins than the one before. Which list shows the first four tables?
questions.explain: The first table has 5, so the list must begin at 5. Then add 10 each time: 5, 15, 25, 35. Beginning at 10 mixes up the start number with the change.

questions.question: Omar has 40 dollars in his jar. He puts in 20 dollars each month. How many dollars are in the jar after 5 months?
questions.explain: Start at 40, then add 20 five times: 60, 80, 100, 120, 140. Count the months on your fingers so you do not add 20 one time too few.

questions.question: On its first trip, a ferry carries 14 cars. Each later trip carries 9 more cars than the trip before. How many cars are on the 4th trip?
questions.explain: Trip 1 is 14, then add 9 for each later trip: 23, 32, 41. The 4th trip has 41 cars, because you add 9 three times, not two.
